The first release of **pcsf**, the reference implementation of the
**Portable Common Subsurface Format** (format version 0.1.0): one
exchange format for electromagnetic and magnetotelluric inversion
models, whatever code produced them.

Every inversion code writes its own format, with its own logarithm
base, axis order, coordinate frame, depth datum and discretization.
PCSF states these conventions in the file, so a model can be read,
checked and compared without knowing the code that made it.

## Install

```bash
pip install pcsf              # core: NumPy + h5py
pip install "pcsf[all]"       # + algorithms, EMC, MARE2DEM, CRS, schemas, Studio
```

## PCSF Studio — download

The desktop application, with installers that need no Python:

| Platform | File |
|---|---|
| Windows 10/11 (64-bit) | `pcsf-studio-0.1.0-setup.exe` (also `pcsf-studio-setup.exe`) |
| Linux (x86-64), portable | `pcsf-studio-0.1.0-x86_64.AppImage` (also `pcsf-studio-x86_64.AppImage`) |
| Linux (x86-64), installs in `~/.local` | `pcsf-studio-0.1.0-linux.sh` (also `pcsf-studio-linux.sh`) |

The files without a version number always point to the latest release.
Windows SmartScreen warns about unsigned installers: choose **More
info → Run anyway**. Check a download against `SHA256SUMS`.

## Highlights

- **Two encodings, one model**: PCSF (HDF5) and PCSM (plain text,
  optionally `.pcsm.gz`) convert into each other bit for bit.
- **What the file holds**: canonical resistivity in linear Ω·m with
  the solver's own values and encoding kept; the native geometry
  (2D grid, 3D grid, triangular mesh or set of profiles), never
  resampled; stations, topography and coordinate reference system;
  and an inversion record (data, errors, regularization, misfit,
  convergence, depth of investigation) with a completeness check.
- **Solver output without the solver**: adapters for Occam2D, ModEM,
  MARE2DEM and the EarthScope Earth Model Collaboration (EMC) netCDF
  archives, on NumPy-only parsers.
- **Checks**: conformance rules C1–C10, JSON Schemas of the metadata,
  and a conformance suite of 27 reference files for independent
  implementations.
- **Algorithms**: sampling, point location on meshes, comparison of
  models, uncertainty propagation and frame registration, NumPy only.
- **Tools**: the `pcsf` command line (`info`, `validate`, `convert`,
  `compare`, `studio`) and **PCSF Studio**, which views and inspects
  models and converts many solver runs to `.pcsf`, `.pcsm` or
  `.pcsm.gz` in one go.
- **Reproducibility**: `paper/` reproduces every number, table and
  figure of the paper that describes the format.
